subject: Executive briefing: Checkoutly impact from QPS thresholding
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] Checkoutly QPS thresholding -> latency increase (initial findings)

Team —

Quick summary: Checkoutly is seeing a persistent p95 increase (~350ms -> ~1.1s) starting 09:05 PDT correlated with their QPS hitting a soft threshold in our routing layer. Early metrics attached (qps-metrics-20260922.csv).

What we've observed so far:
- Spike in steady-state concurrency around 09:02; autoscaler backoff triggered at ~09:04 and did not pop as expected.
- KV cache eviction rate jumped; customer requests causing cold KV hits for identical prefixes.
- When requests fall back to a slow path (quantized model slowpath for seq_len > 1024), per-token time ~2-3x.

Immediate asks:
1) Product: can we temporarily raise the QPS soft threshold for Checkoutly and enable burst capacity? Need decision to proceed within 20m.
2) Eng/SRE (Karthik/Ben): propose emergency routing toggle to prefer warm instances for Checkoutly traffic + increase autoscaler aggressiveness. If you can push a change, call it out and include rollback plan.
3) CS (Grace): prepare a short customer note that acknowledges impact and gives a 90-min mitigation ETA for an initial workaround.

I'm standing by on Slack #ops-bridge.

Attachments: qps-metrics-20260922.csv

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-22T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Checkoutly QPS thresholding -> latency increase (initial findings)

Thanks Ben — this matches what I was seeing in the product dashboards. Two product asks before we change routing: 

- Can we gate the temporary threshold raise to only Checkoutly (account-level override) so we avoid cross-customer regressions?
- If we enable burst capacity, include an explicit budget cap and rollback at 30 minutes if errors/latency don't improve.

Also: higher-level question for roadmap follow-up — KV eviction causing cold hits is recurring for customers with large prompt variability. Can Eng/Research scope a persistent fix (cache prewarming + smarter prefix hashing) and give a 2-week ETA? We'll prioritize on the roadmap if SRE recommends.

Grace, please prepare the 2-line customer note for Olivia with the mitigation ETA Ben suggested and link to the status page.

If Karthik can confirm the routing toggle and budget cap, I'm okay to authorize the account-level threshold override now.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Serving & Reliability
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Checkoutly QPS thresholding -> latency increase (initial findings)

Quick technical readout and proposed mitigation plan: 

Root causes (short):
1) Autoscaler backoff threshold mis-tuned for instances serving long-sequence requests — we saw scale-down decisions at the same time bursty large-seq requests arrived.
2) KV-cache evaporation because several high-cardinality prefixes pushed older entries out; bulk of Checkoutly traffic relied on those cached prefixes.
3) Model slowpath: quantized kernels degrade at sequence lengths above our optimized window due to suboptimal tiling in the current kernel set.

Immediate actions (I can execute):
A) Flip routing rule to prefer warm instance pool for account=Checkoutly. Will add a per-account burst budget capped at 2x baseline QPS; auto-revert after 30 minutes unless SRE extends. ETA: 10 minutes to push and validate. Rollback plan: revert routing flag and evict session affinity.
B) Temporarily increase autoscaler aggressiveness (reduce cooldown and raise target CPU headroom). ETA: 15 minutes; risk: higher infra spend for short window.
C) Start a background job to prewarm KV keys for the top 5 prefixes from the attached CSV. ETA: 45 minutes to seed; will report back when done.

Roadmap asks: we should prioritize a small kernel optimization (tile rewrite) and a targeted cache prewarming feature — estimate 2 sprints for an MVP. Marissa, if you can put this in the Serving backlog as high priority, we can staff it in the next sprint.

I'll push A+B now after Marissa confirms account-level gate.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@checkoutly.com>, support@checkoutly.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-22T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Executive briefing: Checkoutly impact from QPS thresholding

Olivia —

Thank you for your patience this morning and I'm sorry for the disruption. Briefly: at ~09:02 PDT we saw Checkoutly traffic briefly hit a QPS threshold that caused our routing layer to reassign traffic to cooler instances while a subset of your requests also experienced cache misses and entered a slower model execution path. That combination increased median/95 latency for a subset of requests.

What we did (mitigation completed):
- We applied an account-scoped routing override to prefer warm instances for Checkoutly traffic and capped burst at 2x baseline QPS.
- Adjusted autoscaler aggressiveness to avoid premature scale-down during bursty windows.
- Triggered a targeted KV prewarm for the top prefixes that were cold.

Current status: latency metrics are improving; p95 has dropped from ~1.1s to ~420ms for the affected request classes. We're continuing to monitor and will run an expanded validation for the next 3 hours.

Next steps and timeline:
- By EOD PT (within 8 hours): full telemetry sweep and a retrospective note with root cause detail and mitigations.
- Within 72 hours: deploy a prioritized fix (kernel tiling optimization + cache prewarming as a feature) on a canary, then roll out if validation passes.

We will provide a credit for the incident window if you prefer; Grace from CS will coordinate the details. If you'd like a live run-through with our SRE/Engineering leads, we can schedule a 30-minute call today or tomorrow.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/20260922-qps-threshold
Attachments: customer-impact-notes.pdf (short summary), qps-metrics-20260922.csv

Again, really sorry for the interruption — we're treating this as a high priority.

—Dylan Brooks
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0192
